nodes.title: Harish-Chandra's character theorem and the Weyl integration formula over p-adic fields
nodes.statement: Let F be a non-archimedean local field of characteristic 0, G a connected reductive group over F and π an admissible irreducible smooth complex representation of G(F). (a) For f ∈ C_c^∞(G(F)) the operator π(f) has finite rank, and Θ_π(f) = tr π(f) is an invariant distribution. (b) (Harish-Chandra) There is a locally integrable function θ_π on G(F), locally constant on the regular semisimple set G(F)_rs and invariant under conjugation, with Θ_π(f) = ∫_G f(g) θ_π(g) dg for every f; |D^G|^{1/2} θ_π is locally bounded. (c) (Weyl integration formula) For f ∈ C_c^∞(G(F)), ∫_G f(g) dg = Σ_T |N_G(T)(F)/T(F)|^{-1} ∫_{T(F)} |D^G(t)| O_t(f) dt, the sum over representatives T of the G(F)-conjugacy classes of maximal F-tori, with the orbital integrals and measures of ET.1/orbital-integral. (d) Consequently Θ_π(f) = Σ_T |N_G(T)(F)/T(F)|^{-1} ∫_{T(F)} |D^G(t)| θ_π(t) O_t(f) dt, and Θ_π is determined by θ_π on the elliptic regular set together with the characters of proper Levi subgroups through the van Dijk formula for induced representations.
hypotheses: F non-archimedean of characteristic 0 (the theorem is used only in characteristic 0 here).
π admissible and of finite length (irreducible representations are admissible by SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.3a/admissibility-of-irreducibles).
proofSteps: Finite rank of π(f) is admissibility: f is bi-invariant under some compact open K and π(f) factors through π^K.

Clozel 1987 Theorems 1–3: descend an admissible character near a semisimple element to its connected centralizer, use the exponential chart, and express the descended distribution locally by Fourier transforms of nilpotent orbital measures. The discriminant comparison in §3.4 transfers local boundedness/integrability back to the group; ET.1 supplies the orbital Fourier integrability.

The Fourier-support input is Clozel Lemma 6, proved in §§3.5–3.9 from Howe’s small-compact orbit parametrization, the intertwining criterion, the norm estimates and the Fourier coefficient formula. Its underlying Howe theorem and Cartan decomposition are exact character-prefix proof inputs recorded in the gap, not consequences of admissibility.

For the group formula use the Jacobian of (T(F)\G(F)) × T(F)_rs → G(F)_rs, (x,t) ↦ x⁻¹tx: it is |det(1−Ad(t)|𝔤/𝔱)|. Its fibre has |N_G(T)(F)/T(F)| elements. Kottwitz §7 proves the analogous Lie-algebra formula; it does not itself state the group formula.
(d) combines (b) and (c); the formula for parabolically induced characters is van Dijk's, recorded with the induction functor of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.2/parabolic-induction.
acceptance: For G = GL_1, θ_χ = χ for a character χ, and the Weyl integration formula is the identity ∫_{F^×} f = ∫_{F^×} f.
For the Steinberg representation of GL_2(F), θ_St = −1 on the regular elliptic set (a computation used in ET.6/acceptance-examples).
Θ_π is nonzero on C_c^∞(G(F)_rs) for every irreducible π (linear independence of characters).

nodes.title: Twisted characters of θ-stable representations
nodes.statement: Let E/F be a cyclic extension of non-archimedean local fields of characteristic 0 with Gal(E/F) generated by σ, G_0 connected reductive over F and G = R_{E/F}G_0, so σ acts on G(F) = G_0(E). Let Π be an irreducible admissible representation of G_0(E) with Π ≅ Π∘σ, and fix an intertwiner I_σ : Π → Π∘σ (unique up to scalar; with I_σ^ℓ = 1 where ℓ = [E:F]; cyclic base change additionally uses the canonical extension: for generic Π choose the Whittaker-normalized I_σ preserving the fixed Whittaker functional, and for arbitrary Π use the extension induced on its Langlands standard module and its unique irreducible constituent, as in AC Ch. 1 §2 pp. 10–11). (a) The twisted trace f ↦ tr(Π(f) I_σ) on C_c^∞(G_0(E)) is given by a locally integrable function Θ_{Π,σ}, locally constant near σ-regular elements and invariant under σ-conjugacy g ↦ h g σ(h)^{-1}. (b) (Shintani relation, used to define base change; G_0 = GL_n) If γ ∈ GL_n(E) has σ-regular norm Nγ ∈ GL_n(F) (the norm map of AC Ch. 1 §1), the value Θ_{Π,σ}(γ) depends only on the conjugacy class of Nγ; for general G_0 the norm is defined on stable σ-classes (Labesse 1999 §2.5). (c) The twisted Weyl integration formula expresses ∫_{G_0(E)} f in terms of twisted orbital integrals over σ-conjugacy classes, with stable norms for general G_0; the injectivity on rational σ-conjugacy classes asserted here is restricted to GL_n. (d) The same holds for the coset 𝒢θ of a non-connected group 𝒢^+ = 𝒢 ⋊ ⟨θ⟩ with θ of finite order acting by a quasi-semisimple automorphism, which is the form used for the unitary twisted spaces of ET.4/twisted-trace-formula.
hypotheses: F of characteristic 0; Π irreducible admissible and σ-stable.
proofSteps: Apply Clozel 1987 Theorem 1 to the representation of the finite semidirect product obtained from the chosen intertwiner. Restrict its character distribution to the σ-component; the value there is tr(Π(f)I_σ). The discriminant and descent are those of §2 and §3.4, not a formal invocation of the connected theorem.

For GL_n the norm is injective on σ-conjugacy classes by AC Ch. 1 Lemma 1.1(ii), pp. 3–4. Lemma 1.4, pp. 7–8, gives the elliptic norm criterion; the general reductive-group norm correspondence is on stable classes, with rational classes tracked separately.
(d): the same argument applied to the coset of a quasi-semisimple automorphism of finite order.
acceptance: For n = 1, Θ_{χ∘N,σ}(γ) = χ(Nγ) for a character χ of F^× (the norm map is the field norm).
If Π is not σ-stable no twisted character is defined; the statement requires Π ≅ Π∘σ.
Changing I_σ by an ℓ-th root of unity ζ multiplies Θ_{Π,σ} by ζ.

nodes.title: Kottwitz's formula for Tamagawa numbers
nodes.statement: For the connected reductive groups G, their elliptic endoscopic groups H and connected elliptic centralizers I used in this packet, let S be the simply connected cover of the derived group. Kottwitz’s relative formula is τ(G)/τ(S)=|π₀(Z(Ĝ)^Γ)|/|ker¹(k,Z(Ĝ))|. With ET.0/kottwitz-duality and ET.4/classical-simply-connected-tamagawa this gives τ(G)=|π₀(Z(Ĝ)^Γ)|/|ker¹(k,G)|. For G_n⃗ with r positive blocks, the component count is 2^r if [F⁺:ℚ] is even or all blocks are even, and 2^(r−1) otherwise; ker¹ is trivial for these groups. Thus those counts are their Tamagawa numbers, while τ(𝒢_n⃗)=1. The same ratio must be applied to each inner centralizer with its own ker¹; it is not declared trivial merely because it is a centralizer.
hypotheses: Use the Tamagawa measures and split-centre quotient of AA.2. The number-one theorem applies to the simply connected derived cover, not the similitude group.
The displayed absolute formula for the inner-form inputs relies on the explicitly planned classical number-one theorem, whose inner-form proof is a gap.
proofSteps: Use Kottwitz 1984 §5: pass through a z-extension to a group with simply connected derived subgroup, apply Ono’s torus formula and the relative-ratio invariance under the central extension. This supplies τ(G)/τ(S), not τ(S)=1. The absolute number-one input is the separate classical target.
|ker^1(F,G)| = |ker^1(F,Z(Ĝ))| is Kottwitz 1984 (4.2.2), the duality of ET.0/kottwitz-duality.

Shin 2011 Lemma 3.1 pp. 13–14 computes the dual centre and its Γ-fixed component group. Its cohomological argument gives ker¹(G_n⃗)=1; for the base-change group use restriction of scalars, Shapiro and Hilbert 90. Apply the relative formula with the derived covers. Inner centralizers use ET.0 duality separately.
acceptance: τ(𝔾_m) = 1 and τ(R_{F_0/ℚ}𝔾_m) = 1.
τ(U(1)) = 2 for the norm-one torus of an imaginary quadratic F_0 (π_0 of (ℂ^×)^Γ = {±1}, ker^1 trivial).
For n⃗ = (1) and [F^+:ℚ] odd, |π_0(Z(Ĝ_{(1)})^Γ)| = 2^{r−1} = 1 and ker^1 is trivial, so τ(G_{(1)}) = 1 (Shin 2011 Remark 3.2).

nodes.title: The stable elliptic distribution ST^H_e and the coefficient ι(G,H)
nodes.statement: Let (H,s,η) be an elliptic endoscopic triple of a connected reductive ℚ-group G. Work in the space of smooth functions compactly supported modulo A_{H,∞}^0 (the positive real points of the maximal ℚ-split central torus), transforming under a fixed compatible central character χ; all quotient measures and traces use this same convention. For stable-cuspidal h_∞ define ST^H_e(h) = τ(H) Σ_{[γ_H]_st,ell} |π₀(H_{γ_H})(ℚ)|⁻¹ SO_{γ_H}(h), with the connected-centralizer measures and signs specified by Shin 2010 (7.3), p. 26. The coefficient is ι(G,H)=τ(G)τ(H)⁻¹|Out(H,s,η)|⁻¹. For the unitary similitude endoscopic groups in this packet the centralizers are connected, so the component factor is 1.
hypotheses: Only ℚ-elliptic semisimple classes enter; h_∞ must be stable cuspidal so that non-elliptic terms vanish at ∞.
proofSteps: Use the central quotient, support conditions and summation convention of Shin 2010 §1.2 and (7.3). Compactness modulo the entire centre alone does not imply finiteness: a torus would leave all rational central translates. Any finiteness assertion must be made on the specified quotient and support, not inferred from compact support modulo Z(H).
ST^H_e is a stable distribution: each SO_{γ_H} is stable (ET.1/kappa-and-stable-orbital-integrals).
ι(G,H) depends only on the isomorphism class of the triple.
acceptance: For a torus the connected-centralizer component factor is 1, and the formula is τ(T) times the rational sum with A_{T,∞}^0 and the central-character convention fixed; no finiteness follows merely from compact support modulo the whole torus.
For G = G_{2n} and H = G_{n,n}, |Out(H,s,η)| = 2, so ι(G,H) = τ(G)/(2τ(H)).

A semisimple class that is not elliptic at infinity has zero orbital integral against h_∞ stable cuspidal. A sum of stable orbital integrals over more classes remains stable; the ellipticity test checks the selected geometric term, not stability.
For the trivial triple (G,1,id), ι(G,G) = 1.

nodes.title: Kottwitz's stabilization of the elliptic terms
nodes.statement: Let G be connected reductive over ℚ with G_der simply connected, f = ∏_v f_v ∈ C_c^∞(G(𝔸)) with f_∞ the Euler–Poincaré (Lefschetz) function of an irreducible algebraic representation ξ (ET.1/pseudocoefficients). Let T_e(f) = Σ_{γ_0} τ(I_0) · Σ_{γ ∈ adelic class} e(γ) O_γ(f) be the elliptic part of the trace formula written over pairs (γ_0, γ) with γ_0 elliptic semisimple and γ adelically conjugate to γ_0. Then T_e(f) = Σ_{(H,s,η)} ι(G,H) ST^H_e(f^H), the sum over isomorphism classes of elliptic endoscopic triples of G, where f^H = ∏_v f^H_v with f^H_v a transfer of f_v (ET.1/matching-functions, ET.3/local-transfer-existence), f^H_v the unramified image of f_v at almost all v (ET.3/fundamental-lemma-almost-all-places), and f^H_∞ the explicit combination of averaged pseudo-coefficients of ET.1/archimedean-pseudocoefficient-transfer. The ker^1 factors and the κ-sum are those of ET.0/global-kottwitz-obstruction.
hypotheses: G_der simply connected (achieved by a z-extension otherwise)
f_∞ stable cuspidal (Euler–Poincaré), so only elliptic terms occur
transfer factors normalised as a global product equal to 1 on rational pairs (ET.1/transfer-factor-properties)

At infinity use functions compact modulo A_{G,∞}^0 with the central character fixed by ξ, as in Shin 2010 §1.2. For transfers transport that character to the endoscopic and base-change split centres; C_c^∞ in this node denotes this central-character space, not ordinary compact support on the whole group.
Local/global transfer, compatibility and almost-all-place fundamental lemma are supplied by ET.1/ET.3. The simply connected Hasse/Tamagawa inputs of Kottwitz §9.3 are needed for the centralizers.
The full elliptic identity includes the separate central-elliptic-stabilization target. Without that target, the primary theorem establishes only the noncentral identity.
proofSteps: Kottwitz 1986 (9.6.1)–(9.6.4): count rational classes in an adelic stable class via ker¹(I)→ker¹(G), translate the existence condition through the global Kottwitz obstruction and apply finite Fourier inversion in κ.

Use Lemma 9.7 to identify pairs (stable γ,κ) with elliptic endoscopic data and transferred stable classes. Its existence/uniqueness and automorphism-orbit calculation produce the outer automorphism denominator; they are not a simple bijection before taking these orbits.

Apply the transfer-factor product formula and local matching; the cohomological exact-sequence calculation in the proof produces the relative τ₁(G)/τ₁(I) coefficients. Use the number-one target to replace relative Tamagawa numbers by absolute ones.

Theorem 9.6 gives T_e* = Σι ST_e** only: omit central classes on G, use (G,H)-regular classes for proper H, and omit central classes for its quasi-split inner datum. Add the separate complement theorem to obtain the full displayed T_e identity. Its proof remains a recorded gap.

nodes.title: Base-change groups and the L-morphisms BC and ζ̃
nodes.statement: Let F = F^+F_0 be a CM field (F_0 imaginary quadratic, [F^+:ℚ] ≥ 2), n⃗ = (n_1,…,n_s) and G_n⃗ the quasi-split unitary similitude group of ET.0/unitary-elliptic-endoscopic-data, with the character ϖ : 𝔸_{F_0}^×/F_0^× → ℂ^× extending the quadratic character of F_0/ℚ fixed there. Put 𝒢_n⃗ = R_{F_0/ℚ}(G_n⃗ ×_ℚ F_0); then 𝒢_n⃗ ≅ R_{F_0/ℚ}𝔾_m × R_{F/ℚ}GL_n⃗ and its dual group is ℂ^× × ℂ^× × ∏_{σ ∈ Φ} GL_n⃗(ℂ) (Φ the embeddings F → ℂ), W_{F_0} permuting the σ-factors and w ∉ W_{F_0} acting by (λ_+, λ_−, (g_σ)) ↦ (λ_− ∏_{σ ∉ Φ^+} det g_σ, λ_+ ∏_{σ ∈ Φ^+} det g_σ, (Φ_n⃗ ᵗg_{c w^{-1}σ}^{-1} Φ_n⃗^{-1})_σ). The construction gives: (a) the base-change L-morphism BC_n⃗ : ^LG_n⃗ → ^L𝒢_n⃗, (λ,(g_σ)_{σ∈Φ^+}) ⋊ w ↦ (λ, λ, (g_σ)_{σ∈Φ^+}, (g_{cσ})_{σ∉Φ^+}) ⋊ w; (b) for n_1 + n_2 = N the L-morphism ζ̃_{n_1,n_2} : ^L𝒢_{n_1,n_2} → ^L𝒢_N extending GL_{n_1} × GL_{n_2} ⊂ GL_N by the ϖ-twist of η̃_{n_1,n_2} on W_{F_0} and the element (a_{n_1,n_2}, a_{n_1,n_2}, (Φ_{n_1,n_2}Φ_N^{-1})_σ) on a fixed w* ∉ W_{F_0}; (c) the commutative square BC_N ∘ η̃_{n_1,n_2} = ζ̃_{n_1,n_2} ∘ BC_{n_1,n_2}; (d) the automorphism θ of 𝒢_n⃗ induced by the non-trivial element of Gal(F_0/ℚ), θ(λ, g) = (λ^c, λ^c g^♯) with g^♯ = Φ_n⃗ ᵗ(g^c)^{-1} Φ_n⃗^{-1} (the inverse is required; the non-compact sequel §5.5 omits it, see sourceIssues), so that 𝒢_n⃗ ⋊ Gal(F_0/ℚ) ≅ 𝒢^+_n⃗ = 𝒢_n⃗ ⋊ {1, θ}.
hypotheses: F = F^+F_0 CM with F_0 imaginary quadratic; ϖ fixed as in ET.0/unitary-elliptic-endoscopic-data; a_{n_1,n_2} a fixed square root of (−1)^{N(n_1,n_2)} with N(n_1,n_2) = [F^+:ℚ](n_1ε(n_1) + n_2ε(n_2))/2 and ε(m) ∈ {0,1} the parity of m.
proofSteps: Compute the dual group of R_{F_0/ℚ}(G_n⃗)_{F_0} from the Weil-restriction rule (ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.5/dual-of-weil-restriction).
Define BC_n⃗ and ζ̃ by the displayed formulas and check they are L-morphisms by comparing with the action of w ∉ W_{F_0} (Caraiani–Scholze non-compact §5.4, p. 69).
The square (c) commutes by direct computation on Ĝ and on w* (Caraiani–Scholze non-compact (5.4.1), p. 69; Shin 2011 §3.2 and §4.4).
acceptance: The θ-fixed points of 𝒢_n⃗(ℚ) are G_n⃗(ℚ).
The square BC_N ∘ η̃ = ζ̃ ∘ BC holds on W_{F_0} and on w*.
𝒢_n⃗ is not G_n⃗ ×_ℚ F_0 viewed over F_0: it is its Weil restriction to ℚ, whose ℚ-points are G_n⃗(F_0).

nodes.title: Unramified transfers BC*, ζ̃*, η̃* and their compatibilities
nodes.statement: With ET.4/base-change-groups, let v be a place of ℚ outside a finite set S containing ∞, p, ℓ and the primes where F or ϖ ramifies. (a) The L-morphisms BC_n⃗, ζ̃_{n_1,n_2} and η̃_{n_1,n_2} induce, through the Satake isomorphism (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.4/satake-isomorphism), algebra maps BC*_n⃗ : H^ur(𝒢_n⃗(ℚ_v)) → H^ur(G_n⃗(ℚ_v)), ζ̃*_{n_1,n_2} : H^ur(𝒢_N(ℚ_v)) → H^ur(𝒢_{n_1,n_2}(ℚ_v)) and η̃*_{n_1,n_2} : H^ur(G_N(ℚ_v)) → H^ur(G_{n_1,n_2}(ℚ_v)), and dual maps on unramified representations, with tr π(η̃*φ) = tr η̃_*(π)(φ) and the same for BC and ζ̃. (b) The squares BC*_{n_1,n_2} ∘ ζ̃*_{n_1,n_2} = η̃*_{n_1,n_2} ∘ BC*_N on Hecke algebras and the dual square on unramified representations commute. (c) Explicitly, for Q_{n_1,n_2} a parabolic of 𝒢_N with Levi 𝒢_{n_1,n_2}: ζ̃*_{n_1,n_2}(f_v) = f_v^{Q} · χ_{ϖ,v}, the normalised constant term times the character χ_ϖ(λ,g_1,g_2) = ϖ(λ^{−N(n_1,n_2)} ∏_i N_{F/F_0}(det g_i)^{ε(n_i)}), and ζ̃_{n_1,n_2,*}(Π_v) = n-Ind(Π_v ⊗ χ_{ϖ,v}); these formulas extend to all f_v ∈ C_c^∞ and all Π_v ∈ Rep(𝒢_{n_1,n_2}(ℚ_v)), since both groups are products of restrictions of scalars of general linear groups.
hypotheses: v ∉ S for the unramified statements (a),(b); (c) holds at every place v.
proofSteps: (a): functoriality of the Satake isomorphism along L-morphisms between unramified groups (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.4/satake-isomorphism, SR.4/spherical-parameter).
(b): apply (a) to the commutative square of ET.4/base-change-groups (c) (Caraiani–Scholze non-compact (5.4.2)–(5.4.3), from Shin 2011 (4.18)).
(c): the constant-term formula tr π(f^Q) = tr n-Ind(π)(f) and its unramified version (Shin 2011 Lemma 3.3), with the twist by χ_ϖ read off from ζ̃ (Caraiani–Scholze non-compact Remark 5.4.1).
acceptance: For v split in F_0, BC*_n⃗ is surjective (Shin 2011 §4.2, Case 2).
For n_2 = 0, ζ̃* is the identity.
tr(n-Ind(Π ⊗ χ_ϖ))(f) = tr Π(f^Q · χ_ϖ) for f ∈ C_c^∞(𝒢_N(ℚ_v)) (constant-term adjunction).

nodes.title: Base-change transfer of test functions at every place
nodes.statement: With ET.4/base-change-groups: (a) (split places) if v splits in F_0 (in particular v = p in the applications), every f_v ∈ C_c^∞(𝒢_n⃗(ℚ_v)) has a BC-transfer φ_v ∈ C_c^∞(G_n⃗(ℚ_v)) (Shin 2011 §4.2, Case 2), i.e. tr π_v(φ_v) = tr(BC(π_v)(f_v) ∘ A_θ) for the normalised θ-intertwiner, and the map f_v ↦ φ_v is surjective onto C_c^∞(G_n⃗(ℚ_v)); base change of irreducible representations at such v is injective. (b) (all finite places; Labesse 1999 Théorème 3.3.1) every f_v ∈ C_c^∞(𝒢_n⃗(ℚ_v)) has a φ_v with matching orbital integrals, i.e. SO_γ(φ_v) equals the stable twisted orbital integral of f_v at δ when γ is a norm of δ, and SO_γ(φ_v) = 0 when γ is not a norm. (c) (inverse transfer; Labesse 1999 Proposition 3.3.2) a function φ_v ∈ C_c^∞(G_n⃗(ℚ_v)) whose stable orbital integrals vanish at every semisimple element that is not a norm is a BC-transfer of some f_v. (d) (norm criterion) a semisimple γ ∈ G_n⃗(ℚ_v) is a norm iff its image in the cocentre D_n⃗ = G_n⃗/G_n⃗^der is a norm; for v split in F_0 every element is a norm (Caraiani–Scholze non-compact Lemma 5.4.3, via Labesse 1999 Proposition 2.5.3).
hypotheses: v finite; in (c),(d) v may be inert or ramified in F_0.
proofSteps: (a): at split v, 𝒢_n⃗(ℚ_v) ≅ G_n⃗(ℚ_v) × G_n⃗(ℚ_v) with θ swapping factors; take φ_v the convolution of the two components (Shin 2011 §4.2, Case 2).

(b),(c): Labesse's transfer for stable base change, the twisted analogue of ET.3/local-transfer-existence, recorded at ET.3/base-change-fundamental-lemma-and-transfer (c); Proposition 3.3.2 is its converse for functions supported on norms.

(d): Labesse 1999 Proposition 2.5.3 reduces to the cocentre of an elliptic Levi M containing γ; the explicit description of D_n⃗ and D_M as tori with multiplier λ shows that an element of D_M is a norm iff its image in D_n⃗ is (Caraiani–Scholze non-compact proof of Lemma 5.4.3, after Morel 2010 Lemma 8.3.6).
acceptance: At split v, with vol(K) = 1, the BC-transfer of 1_K ⊗ 1_K is 1_K.
For n⃗ = (1) the norm criterion reduces to the classical criterion for the multiplier torus.
A function supported on non-norms has BC-transfer 0 under (b).

nodes.title: Small-level functions are base-change transfers (the level N_0)
nodes.statement: Let S_pf be a finite set of finite primes at which F_0 need not be split. For every v ∈ S_pf there is an open neighbourhood U_v of 1 in G_N(ℚ_v) such that every φ_v ∈ C_c^∞(G_N(ℚ_v)) supported in U_v has the property that, for each elliptic endoscopic G_n⃗ of G_N and each Langlands–Shelstad transfer φ_v^n⃗ of φ_v to G_n⃗(ℚ_v), φ_v^n⃗ is the BC-transfer of some f_v^n⃗ ∈ C_c^∞(𝒢_n⃗(ℚ_v)). Consequently there is an integer N_0 ≥ 3 divisible only by primes in S_pf such that, for every N divisible by N_0, the characteristic function of the principal congruence subgroup K(N)_v has this property at every v ∈ S_pf, and every sufficiently small compact open subgroup is transferable in the sense of Liu–Tian–Xiao–Zhang–Zhu Definition D.2.1.
hypotheses: v ∈ S_pf finite; the elliptic endoscopic groups are those of ET.0/unitary-elliptic-endoscopic-data.
proofSteps: By ET.4/base-change-transfer-of-functions (d), there is a neighbourhood U_n⃗ of 1 in G_n⃗(ℚ_v) all of whose semisimple elements are norms, because norms in a torus contain a neighbourhood of 1.
Morel 2010 Lemma 8.4.2 gives a neighbourhood V_n⃗ of 1 in G_N(F_0 ⊗ ℚ_v) such that semisimple elements of G_n⃗(ℚ_v) conjugate into V_n⃗ are conjugate into U_n⃗; intersect over the finitely many n⃗.

If SO_γ(φ^n⃗) ≠ 0 then γ matches some δ with O_δ(φ) ≠ 0, so δ ∈ U and γ is conjugate into U_n⃗, hence a norm; conclude by ET.4/base-change-transfer-of-functions (c) (Caraiani–Scholze non-compact proof of Lemma 5.4.4, after Morel 2010 Lemma 8.4.1).
acceptance: For v split in F_0, U_v = G_N(ℚ_v) works.
When every prime of S_pf splits in F_0, every level satisfies the transfer condition.
The constant function 1_{G_N(ℤ_v)} need not be transferable in this sense at a ramified v; small support is a genuine hypothesis.

nodes.title: Archimedean Euler–Poincaré and twisted Lefschetz functions for unitary similitude groups
nodes.statement: Let G be a unitary similitude group over ℚ that is an inner form of G_N at ∞ of arbitrary signature, ξ an irreducible algebraic representation of G_ℂ, and Ξ = ξ ⊗ ξ the corresponding representation of (𝒢_n⃗)_ℂ. Construct: (a) the Euler–Poincaré function φ_{G_n⃗,ξ} (ET.1/pseudocoefficients) and Labesse's twisted Lefschetz function f_{𝒢_n⃗,Ξ} ∈ C_c^∞(𝒢_n⃗(ℝ)), whose twisted traces compute twisted Lefschetz numbers of (𝔤,K)-cohomology; they are BC-matching; (b) for each elliptic endoscopic G_n⃗ of G, the function φ^n⃗_∞ = e_n⃗(Δ_∞)(−1)^{q(G)}⟨μ_h, s⟩ Σ_{φ_H} det(ω_*(φ_H)) φ_{φ_H}, the sum over discrete L-parameters φ_H of G_n⃗ with η̃_n⃗ ∘ φ_H equivalent to the parameter of ξ, φ_{φ_H} the averaged pseudo-coefficient of the packet and q(G) = ½ dim G(ℝ)/K_∞A_{G,∞}^0; (c) the twisted analogue f^n⃗_∞ = e_n⃗(Δ_∞)(−1)^{q(G)}⟨μ_h, s⟩ Σ_{φ_n⃗} det(ω_*(φ_n⃗)) f_{𝒢_n⃗,Ξ(φ_n⃗)}; then f^n⃗_∞ and φ^n⃗_∞ are BC-matching, and φ^n⃗_∞ is a transfer of the Euler–Poincaré function of G (Kottwitz's construction, ET.1/archimedean-pseudocoefficient-transfer). In the pure U(p,q) factor construct the coefficient F=E⊗θE with θ acting by interchange of the two factors. With the Euler–Poincaré measure, Clozel–Labesse 2011 Theorems 4.1/5.1 give SO_δ(f_F)=0 when I_δ has no discrete series, and otherwise SO_δ(f_F)=e(I_δ)2^n tr(E(γ)) for γ=gθ(g), δ=gθ in GL_n(ℂ)θ. The centralizer sign e(I_δ) is essential, including at singular semisimple δ. For restrictions of scalars and similitude centres transport the factor formula with the split-centre measures and the ET.1 transfer normalization; the pure-unitary formula is not asserted unchanged for GU.
hypotheses: G_ℝ an inner form of G_N of arbitrary signature (not only Harris–Taylor signature); ξ irreducible algebraic; the sign e_n⃗(Δ_∞) and ⟨μ_h,s⟩ fixed by the transfer-factor normalisation of ET.1/transfer-factor-properties.

At infinity use functions compact modulo A_{G,∞}^0 with the central character fixed by ξ, as in Shin 2010 §1.2. For transfers transport that character to the endoscopic and base-change split centres; C_c^∞ in this node denotes this central-character space, not ordinary compact support on the whole group.
proofSteps: Clozel–Labesse 2011 Theorem 2.2 constructs the Lefschetz trace distribution from the K-supported distribution and a Paley–Wiener regularizing multiplier with value one at the coefficient parameter. Lemma 3.2 makes its semisimple orbital integrals independent of regularization; Proposition 3.3 gives the regular orbital formula. Theorems 4.1/5.1 use connected-centralizer Euler–Poincaré functions to obtain the singular stable formula with e(I_δ). The published correction on p. 115 repairs the omitted sign in Labesse 1999 Appendix A.
(b): Shin 2011 (5.11), p. 35, with the real endoscopic signs of Shin 2011 §3.6; for arbitrary signature use q(G) and the packets of G_ℝ (Caraiani–Scholze 2017 §5.2 p. 735 and §5.3 pp. 737–738).
(c): Shin 2011 (6.7), p. 43; BC-matching of f^n⃗_∞ and φ^n⃗_∞ follows termwise from (a).

Use Shin §4.3 and ET.1’s real packet transfer for the pure-unitary norm correspondence and then transport products and the common similitude split centre with the chosen central character. The required quotient-measure and real-character boundary proof inputs are recorded explicitly.
acceptance: If G(ℝ)/A_{G,∞}^0 is compact and ξ=1 with trivial central character, its normalized constant function represents the Euler–Poincaré trace. Compactness merely modulo the full centre does not imply this assertion.

For arbitrary signature recompute q(G), the Shimura cocharacter μ_h, the pairing ⟨μ_h,s⟩ and the contributing real packets. Holding μ_h fixed while changing signature need not preserve the endoscopic coefficients.
For the trivial triple the coefficient is (−1)^{q(G)}.

On a compact real quotient choose ξ and a coefficient Ξ′ whose restriction along the base-change embedding has a different highest weight and no ξ-constituent. Schur orthogonality distinguishes their traces and prevents matching; mere inequality Ξ′≠ξ⊗ξ is insufficient.
Choose a semisimple δ with e(I_δ)=−1 and nonzero coefficient trace. The pure-unitary stable orbital integral is −2^n tr ξ(gθ(g)), distinguishing the corrected formula from the unsigned one.

nodes.title: The invariant twisted trace formula for the unitary base-change spaces
nodes.statement: On the component 𝒢_n⃗θ of 𝒢_n⃗⋊⟨θ⟩, the invariant global formula equates I_geom(fθ) and I_spec(fθ). Use fixed-central-character functions compact modulo the specified positive real split centre; restrict to 𝒢(𝔸)¹ after the central-character twist, as in Shin §4.5. The geometric expansion is the sum over Levi subsets and rational classes of Arthur’s coefficients times the invariant twisted orbital distributions; the spectral expansion is the sum over discrete inducing data and intertwiner terms of the invariant twisted character distributions. The precise distributions are ET.4/twisted-invariant-distributions. The ordered spectral limit is Arthur II Theorem 6.4; no unproved absolute convergence of a doubly indexed sum is asserted. Splitting and descent are part of the same component theory.
hypotheses: 𝒢^+_n⃗ is a non-connected group whose coset 𝒢θ is defined by an automorphism θ of order 2 preserving a ℚ-splitting; f has the stated central character.

At infinity use functions compact modulo A_{G,∞}^0 with the central character fixed by ξ, as in Shin 2010 §1.2. For transfers transport that character to the endoscopic and base-change split centres; C_c^∞ in this node denotes this central-character space, not ordinary compact support on the whole group.

nodes.title: Local cyclic base change for GL_n (Arthur–Clozel)
nodes.statement: Let E/F be a cyclic extension of non-archimedean local fields of characteristic 0 of prime degree ℓ with Gal(E/F) = ⟨σ⟩, and G = GL_n. (Definition, Shintani) For tempered representations, a σ-stable irreducible admissible representation Π of GL_n(E) is a base-change lift of an irreducible admissible π of GL_n(F) if Θ_{Π,σ}(g) = Θ_π(Ng) for every g ∈ GL_n(E) with σ-regular norm Ng, the twisted character normalised as in ET.4/twisted-characters. Then (all representations induced from cuspidal): (a) if π is cuspidal and π ≇ π⊗ω, there is a unique σ-stable Π lifting π, and Π is cuspidal; (b) if π is cuspidal and π ≅ π⊗ω, then ℓ divides n and Π is the isobaric sum of the ℓ distinct conjugates of a cuspidal representation of GL_{n/ℓ}(𝔸_E); (c) every σ-stable cuspidal Π is the lift of some cuspidal π, unique up to twisting by powers of ω; (d) a weak lift is a strong lift; (e) ω_Π = ω_π ∘ N_{E/F}, and the lift is independent of the choice of σ; (f) two cuspidal π, π′ with the same lift differ by a power of ω. nodes.title: Cyclic automorphic induction for GL_n (Arthur–Clozel)
nodes.statement: Let E/F be a cyclic extension of number fields of degree ℓ (prime or not) and π_E an automorphic representation of GL_m(𝔸_E) induced from cuspidal. Say that an automorphic representation π_F of GL_{mℓ}(𝔸_F) is automorphically induced from π_E if at almost all places v unramified in E, the Satake parameter of π_{F,v} is the induction of those of π_{E,w}: at v split in E it is the direct sum over w | v, and at an arbitrary unramified v it is ⊕_{w|v} Ind_{W_{E_w}}^{W_{F_v}}. Then there exists one and only one such π_F, and π_F is induced from cuspidal. For ℓ prime and π_E cuspidal, π_F is cuspidal iff π_E is not isomorphic to its Galois conjugate π_E^σ; the induction is transitive along towers of cyclic extensions; and its base change to E is the isobaric sum of the Galois conjugates of π_E.

Tempered local parameters have the relevant packets and inner-twist pairings of Theorem* 1.6.1; general localizations of a generic global parameter require the extended packet construction and are not asserted tempered. nodes.title: Transfer between GSp_4 and GL_4 for general-type representations
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field, Π a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_4(𝔸_F) and χ : 𝔸_F^×/F^× → ℂ^× unitary with Π ≅ Π^∨ ⊗ (χ∘det). Exactly one of L^S(s, Π, ∧² ⊗ χ^{-1}) and L^S(s, Π, Sym² ⊗ χ^{-1}) has a pole at s = 1; in the first (symplectic) case Π descends to a discrete automorphic representation π of GSp_4(𝔸_F) with central character χ, and in the second to a discrete representation of the quasi-split quadratic form GSpin_4^α prescribed by its orthogonal parameter. A discrete π of GSp_4 arising this way is of general type; it is cuspidal and stable, every π′ with π′_v in the L-packet of π_v for all v is automorphic and occurs with multiplicity one, the L-parameter of π_v composed with GSp_4 ⊂ GL_4 is rec(Π_v), and if π is algebraic then Π is algebraic (the forward implication stated in BCGP §1.8.22).

nodes.title: Acceptable elements of J_b(ℚ_p) and acceptable test functions
nodes.statement: Let (B, O_B, *, V, Λ_0, ⟨,⟩, h) be an unramified integral PEL datum of type (A) or (C) with group G, p a good prime, b ∈ B(G_{ℚ_p}, −μ) and Σ_b a completely slope-divisible p-divisible group with G-structure of type b, with slope decomposition Σ_b = ⊕_{i=1}^r Σ_i of slopes λ_1 > … > λ_r, so J_b(ℚ_p) ⊂ ∏_i End^0(Σ_i)^× (IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration:IG.0/automorphism-group-of-universal-cover). (a) An element δ = (δ_i) ∈ J_b(ℚ_p) is acceptable if for all i < j every eigenvalue e_i of δ_i and e_j of δ_j satisfy v_p(e_i) < v_p(e_j). More generally, for a Levi M_0 ⊂ G_0 with central cocharacter ν, a semisimple γ ∈ M_0(ℚ_p) is ν-acceptable if for every root α of G_0 not in M_0, ⟨α,ν⟩ > 0 iff α(γ) has positive p-adic valuation (Shin 2010 Definition 3.1); with the sign convention for the cocharacter attached to b in Shin 2010 §3.2, this agrees with (a) (Remark 3.3). nodes.title: The fixed-point formula for Frobenius-twisted Igusa correspondences
nodes.statement: Let φ = 1_{U^p(m) g U^p(m)} with g ∈ G(𝔸_f^p) × S_b, U^p(m) small, and Ig_{b,U^p,m} the finite-level Igusa variety over 𝔽̄_p with a model over a finite field 𝔽_{p^s} on which the absolute Frobenius acts as fr^{-s} ∈ J_b(ℚ_p). (a) The double coset defines an algebraic correspondence [U^p(m) g U^p(m)] on Ig_{b,U^p,m} through a smaller level V^p(m′), and a cohomological correspondence on L_ξ. (b) There is M′ > 0, independent of the coefficient sheaf, such that for every N > M′ the correspondence (Fr^s × 1)^N ∘ [U^p(m) g U^p(m)] = [U^p(m) g (fr^{-s})^N U^p(m)] has finitely many fixed points and its Lefschetz trace on H_c(Ig_{b,U^p,m}, L_ξ) equals the sum over its fixed points of the traces on the stalks of L_ξ. (c) Consequently φ^{(N)}(x) = φ(x·(fr^s)^N) is acceptable for N ≫ 0 (Shin 2009 Lemma 6.3). For a normalized double-coset function e_g=1_{UgU}/vol(U), the trace is the correspondence trace; for the unnormalized characteristic function 1_{UgU}, multiply the correspondence fixed-point sum by vol(U), as in Shin 2009 (11), p. 17.

nodes.title: Segments of cuspidal representations and their linking
nodes.statement: Let F be a non-archimedean local field of characteristic 0 and ν = |det| the unramified character of every GL_d(F). Let C be the set of isomorphism classes of irreducible supercuspidal representations of the groups GL_d(F), d ≥ 1. A segment is a finite set Δ = [ρ, ν^{k−1}ρ] = {ρ, νρ, …, ν^{k−1}ρ} ⊂ C with ρ ∈ C and k ≥ 1; its length is k, its degree kd, its beginning ρ and its end ν^{k−1}ρ. In the real-endpoint convention of Atobe–Kondo–Yasuda, [a,b]_ρ with b − a ∈ ℤ_{≥0} denotes {ν^a ρ, …, ν^b ρ}, presentations differing by an unramified twist that fixes ρ being identified. Two segments Δ_1, Δ_2 are linked if Δ_1 ∪ Δ_2 is a segment and neither contains the other; if they are linked, Δ_1 precedes Δ_2 if the beginning of Δ_2 is ν^j times the beginning of Δ_1 with j > 0; they are juxtaposed if Δ_1 ∩ Δ_2 = ∅ and Δ_1 ∪ Δ_2 is a segment. A multisegment is a finite multiset of segments; its degree is the sum of the degrees.

ρ supercuspidal (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.3a/cuspidal-representations)

A segment of length 1 is linked to {νρ} and {ν^{-1}ρ} and to no other segment of length 1.
[1, ν²] and [ν] are not linked although their union is a segment.
No segment precedes itself and precedence is asymmetric.

nodes.title: Representations attached to segments: Zelevinsky, Steinberg and Speh representations
nodes.statement: For a segment Δ = [ρ, ν^{k−1}ρ] with ρ a supercuspidal representation of GL_d(F), the normalised parabolic induction ρ × νρ × … × ν^{k−1}ρ of GL_{kd}(F) has a unique irreducible subrepresentation Z(Δ) = ⟨Δ⟩ and a unique irreducible quotient L(Δ). L(Δ) is essentially square-integrable, and every essentially square-integrable irreducible representation of GL_n(F) is L(Δ) for a unique segment (Bernstein). For ρ = χ a character of GL_1, Z([χ, ν^{k−1}χ]) is the character χν^{(k−1)/2}∘det and L([χ, ν^{k−1}χ]) is the twisted Steinberg representation St_k(χν^{(k−1)/2}). For an irreducible tempered π of GL_n(F) and m ≥ 1, the Speh representation Sp(π, m) is the unique irreducible subrepresentation of π ν^{−(m−1)/2} × … × π ν^{(m−1)/2}; for π = L(Δ) square-integrable and unitary it is Tadić's u(π, m), the unique irreducible quotient of ν^{(m−1)/2}π × … × ν^{−(m−1)/2}π.

nodes.title: Zelevinsky and Langlands classifications of irreducible representations of GL_n
nodes.statement: (a) If Δ_1, …, Δ_r are segments ordered so that Δ_i does not precede Δ_j for i < j, then Z(Δ_1) × … × Z(Δ_r) has a unique irreducible subrepresentation Z(m), depending only on the multisegment m = {Δ_1, …, Δ_r}, and L(Δ_1) × … × L(Δ_r) has a unique irreducible quotient L(m); m ↦ Z(m) and m ↦ L(m) are bijections from multisegments of degree n to irreducible representations of GL_n(F). (b) Z(Δ_1) × … × Z(Δ_r) is irreducible iff no two Δ_i are linked; the same for the L(Δ_i). (c) Every irreducible generic representation is L(Δ_1) × … × L(Δ_r) with pairwise unlinked segments, the multiset being unique; such products are generic. (d) Z(m)^∨ = Z(m^∨) with m^∨ the multisegment of contragredient segments; the highest derivative of Z(m) is Z(m^−), m^− obtained by truncating each segment at its end; Z(m_1 + … + m_p) occurs with multiplicity one in Z(m_1) × … × Z(m_p). (e) There is an involution m ↦ m^# (Zelevinsky's involution, computed by the Mœglin–Waldspurger algorithm) with L(m) = Z(m^#). (f) The cuspidal support of Z(m) and of L(m) is the multiset union of the segments; L(m) is the Langlands quotient of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.3/langlands-classification with essentially square-integrable data L(Δ_i).

For (e), AKY §2.3 pp. 7–8 records the dual and references a later proof. nodes.title: Tadić's classification of the unitary dual and the generic unitary representations
nodes.statement: Let D^u be the set of unitary square-integrable irreducible representations of the GL_m(F), m ≥ 1, and B = {u(δ, n), ν^α u(δ, n) × ν^{−α} u(δ, n) : δ ∈ D^u, n ≥ 1, 0 < α < ½}. (a) Every product of elements of B is irreducible and unitary. (b) Every irreducible unitary representation of GL_n(F) is such a product, uniquely up to order. (c) In particular every irreducible generic unitary representation is irreducibly induced from τ_1 ν^{α_1} ⊗ … ⊗ τ_d ν^{α_d} ⊗ τ_0 ⊗ τ_d ν^{−α_d} ⊗ … ⊗ τ_1 ν^{−α_1} with τ_i unitary generic tempered and ½ > α_1 > … > α_d > 0 (the complementary-series exponents lie in (0, ½)), and a conjugate self-dual generic unitary representation of GL_a over a quadratic extension has this form with τ_i^* in the second half.

All complementary-series exponents α and α_i are real; products use normalized induction.

(c): restrict to generic members, where by ET.6/zelevinsky-classification (c) only n = 1 occurs in u(δ, n); this is the form used in Jiang–Zhang 2020 Appendix B, (B.5)–(B.6).

nodes.title: Weil–Deligne parameters of segments and multisegments
nodes.statement: Use the Weil–Deligne representations of ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/weil-deligne-representation over ℂ (or ℚ̄_ℓ via a fixed isomorphism), with |·| : W_F → ℝ_{>0} sending geometric Frobenius to q^{−1}. Import the unnormalised special object ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/unnormalised-special-object: for k ≥ 1, Sp_k = ⊕_{i=0}^{k−1} ℂ e_i with r(w)e_i = |w|^i e_i and N e_i = e_{i+1} (N e_{k−1} = 0); then r(w) N r(w)^{-1} = |w| N, N is a single Jordan block, and Sp_k is indecomposable and Frobenius-semisimple. nodes.title: Functorial extensions of local class field theory and Henniart's characterization
nodes.statement: A family π↦σ_F(π) of n-dimensional semisimple W_F-representations, for all finite F/ℚ_p and all n≥1, is a functorial extension of class field theory if it is natural under field isomorphisms and satisfies Scholze Theorem 12.1: (i) rank one is local reciprocity with geometric Frobenius; (ii) a subquotient of normalized induction has the direct sum of the inducing parameters; (iii) twisting by χ∘det tensors the parameter with σ_F(χ); (iv) prime-degree cyclic base change of a supercuspidal π restricts its parameter to W_E; (v) if σ_F(π) is unramified, π has an Iwahori-fixed vector. The existing ClassFieldTheory roadmap uses arithmetic reciprocity; define Art_geo(x)=Art_arith(x⁻¹) in W_F^ab, so (i) means σ_F(χ)=χ∘Art_geo⁻¹. Determinants and duals are later conclusions, not substitute axioms for (v). Henniart’s uniqueness characterization by factors of pairs is a separate target, requiring the factor comparison of ET.6/l-epsilon-of-pairs.
hypotheses: F a finite extension of ℚ_p; Art_F normalised by geometric Frobenius
proofSteps: Use exactly Theorem 12.1 and Definition 12.2, Scholze pp. 30–31. Condition (v) drives the finite base-change induction in Theorem 12.3. Transport the existing arithmetic reciprocity normalization by inversion in the abelian target; no inversion map on the nonabelian Weil group is asserted.
The additional uniqueness theorem uses equality of L and ε of supercuspidal pairs, as recalled in Scholze §1 p. 2; its primary proof remains to be supplied.
acceptance: For n = 1 the unique family is local class field theory with geometric Frobenius normalisation.
Normalising Art_F by arithmetic Frobenius gives a family violating (i) as stated (it is the contragredient family).
On unramified principal series the family gives the sum of the unramified characters with the Satake parameters of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.4/spherical-parameter.
With the fixed normalized σ and geometric Frobenius, σ_F(St₂)=|·|^(−1/2)⊕|·|^(1/2), not 1⊕|·|. It is unramified and St₂ has Iwahori-fixed vectors.

nodes.title: Deformation spaces of one-dimensional ϖ-divisible O-modules with Drinfeld level structure
nodes.statement: Let F/ℚ_p be finite with ring of integers O, uniformizer ϖ and residue field 𝔽_q, F_r the unramified extension of degree r with ring O_r, and ŎF the completion of the maximal unramified extension. A ϖ-divisible O-module over a scheme S on which p is locally nilpotent is a p-divisible group H with an O-action whose two induced actions on Lie H agree. For β ∈ GL_n(O_r) diag(ϖ, 1, …, 1) GL_n(O_r), let H_β be the one-dimensional ϖ-divisible O-module of height n over 𝔽_{q^r} determined by β (its Dieudonné module has σ-semilinear Frobenius F=βσ). (a) The formal deformation space R_β of H_β (as ϖ-divisible O-module) is formally smooth, isomorphic to O_r[[T_1, …, T_{n−1}]]. (b) For m ≥ 0 the covering R_{β,m} parametrising Drinfeld level-m structures (sections X_1, …, X_n of the universal deformation forming a full set of sections of its ϖ^m-torsion in Drinfeld's sense) is regular, finite over R_β and Galois with group GL_n(O/ϖ^m), étale in the generic fibre. (c) R_{β,m} algebraises: there is a separated flat scheme of finite type over O_r with smooth generic fibre and GL_n(O/ϖ^m)-action with a finite stable special-fibre subscheme Z such that its completion along Z is R_{β,m}. (d) The nearby-cycle cohomology H^0(R^iψ Spf R_{β,m}, ℚ̄_ℓ) is a finite-dimensional continuous representation of W_{F_r} × GL_n(O/ϖ^m), zero outside 0 ≤ i ≤ n−1.
hypotheses: F of characteristic 0 (p-divisible groups do not exist in the equal-characteristic analogue with the same hypotheses)
ℓ ≠ p
H_β one-dimensional of height n
proofSteps: (a),(b): Drinfeld's theory of level structures (Drinfeld 1974), as recalled in Scholze 2010 Definition 2.2 and Proposition 2.3; the deformation theory of p-divisible groups is that of FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.2.
(c): Scholze 2010 Theorem 2.4, constructing ℛ_{β,m} from moduli of Drinfeld level structures.

(d): Scholze 2010 Theorem 2.5 (Berkovich's nearby cycles for formal schemes; ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:formal-adic-comparison and LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles:LPV.6), independence of ℓ by Mieda.
acceptance: For n = 1, R_{β,m} is the ring of integers of the level-m Lubin–Tate extension over F_r.
For n=1, q>2 and m=1, the Lubin–Tate torsion extension has ramification degree q−1>1; its integral cover is not étale. The blanket claim for all m≥1 would fail when q=2,m=1.
R_β has Krull dimension n, i.e. relative dimension n − 1 over O_r, the dimension of the Lubin–Tate space.

nodes.title: Scholze's test functions φ_{τ,h} and f_{τ,h}
nodes.statement: Fix ℓ ≠ p, τ ∈ Frob^r I_F ⊂ W_F with r ≥ 1 (Frob geometric) and h ∈ C_c^∞(GL_n(O)) with values in ℚ, and set h^∨(g) = h(ᵗg^{-1}). Define φ_{τ,h} on GL_n(F_r) by φ_{τ,h}(β) = tr(τ × h^∨ | [Rψ_β]) for β ∈ GL_n(O_r) diag(ϖ,1,…,1) GL_n(O_r), where [Rψ_β] is the alternating sum of the nearby-cycle cohomology of R_{β,m} for m large enough that h is bi-invariant under 1 + ϖ^m M_n(O) (ET.6/drinfeld-level-deformation-spaces (d)), and φ_{τ,h}(β) = 0 for other β. Then φ_{τ,h} ∈ C_c^∞(GL_n(F_r)) takes values in ℚ and is independent of ℓ. Let f_{τ,h} ∈ C_c^∞(GL_n(F)) be a function with matching (twisted) orbital integrals: the orbital integrals of f_{τ,h} at regular elements equal the σ-twisted orbital integrals of φ_{τ,h} at elements with that norm, and vanish at non-norms (ET.4/local-cyclic-base-change; ET.6/norm-maps-and-base-change-identities). f_{τ,h} is not unique, but its orbital integrals and its traces on representations are well defined.
hypotheses: F finite over ℚ_p; r ≥ 1 so that τ lies over a positive power of geometric Frobenius
h ℚ-valued and conjugation-invariant enough that h^∨ acts
proofSteps: Local constancy in β follows from the algebraisation and the finite group action (Scholze 2010 Theorem 2.4, Theorem 2.6 proof); compact support from the double-coset condition.
Rationality and independence of ℓ: Mieda's theorem (Scholze 2010 Theorem 2.6).
Existence of f_{τ,h}: the base change of functions for GL_n along the unramified extension F_r/F (Arthur–Clozel Ch. 1 §3, Proposition 3.1; ET.3/base-change-fundamental-lemma-and-transfer (c)).
acceptance: For n = 1, tr(f_{τ,h} | χ) = χ(Art_F^{-1}(τ)) tr(h | χ): Theorem 1.2(a) for n = 1 is local class field theory.
At any fixed β and τ, φ_{τ,h₁+h₂}(β)=φ_{τ,h₁}(β)+φ_{τ,h₂}(β), and φ_{τ,0}=0. This tests the linear trace construction without importing an unread comparison with Kottwitz’s spherical function.
φ_{τ,h}(1) = 0, since 1 is not in the double coset of diag(ϖ,1,…,1).
Two choices of f_{τ,h} may differ as functions; only their orbital integrals and traces are determined.

nodes.title: Norm maps for D-groups and base-change identities for the test functions
nodes.statement: Let D be a semisimple algebra over ℚ_p with maximal order O_D. (a) There is a bijection β ↦ Nβ between (O_D ⊗ ℤ_{p^r})^×-σ_0-conjugacy classes in (O_D ⊗ ℤ_{p^r})^× and O_D^×-conjugacy classes in O_D^×, under which the characteristic polynomial of Nβ equals that of β β^{σ_0} ⋯ β^{σ_0^{r−1}}; for h on O_D^× conjugation-invariant, the function φ_h(β) = h(Nβ) on (O_D ⊗ ℤ_{p^r})^× has matching twisted orbital integrals with h, and ∫ φ_h = ∫ h (Scholze 2010 Proposition 4.2, Proposition 4.3, Corollary 4.5). (b) For the height-n infinitesimal one-dimensional ϖ-divisible O-module, let B_r be the basic elements in GL_n(O_r)diag(ϖ,1,…,1)GL_n(O_r), and let D_r be the elements of valuation r in the central division algebra of invariant 1/n, with valuation of a division uniformizer 1. There is a norm correspondence between σ-conjugacy classes in B_r and conjugacy classes in D_r, with the associated orbital and integral identities (Proposition 4.6, Proposition 4.7, Corollary 4.8). For D = M_n(ℚ_p) and h = 1_{GL_n(ℤ_p)} this is the usual base-change identity for the unit element.
hypotheses: semisimple D over ℚ_p with maximal order; unramified extension of degree r
proofSteps: Interpret σ_0-conjugacy classes as isomorphism classes of D-groups (étale p-divisible groups with O_D^op-action) over 𝔽_{p^r} and Nβ as the Frobenius over 𝔽_p (Scholze 2010 Definition 4.1, §4).
Matching of twisted orbital integrals: compare the counting of D-groups over 𝔽_{p^r} and over 𝔽_p (Proposition 4.3, Remark 4.4).
The integral identities follow from the Weyl integration formula (ET.4/padic-character-distributions, ET.4/twisted-characters).
acceptance: For D = ℚ_p, N is the norm from ℤ_{p^r}^× to ℤ_p^×.
For D = M_n(ℚ_p) and h = 1_{GL_n(ℤ_p)}, φ_h = 1_{GL_n(ℤ_{p^r})}, the unit base-change identity (ET.3/base-change-fundamental-lemma-and-transfer (a)).
∫ φ_h = ∫ h is the case of the identity term.

nodes.title: Geometric and harmonic descent for the test functions
nodes.statement: (a) (Geometric descent) The connected components of Spf(R_{β,m} ⊗ Ŏ) are parametrised by surjective O-linear maps (O/ϖ^m)^n → H_β^{ét}[ϖ^m](k̄), with GL_n(O/ϖ^m) acting transitively; the nearby cycles of R_{β,m} decompose accordingly along the connected–étale filtration (Scholze 2010 Proposition 5.1). (b) (Harmonic descent) For π the normalised parabolic induction of π_1 ⊗ … ⊗ π_t (t ≥ 2) of a Levi GL_{n_1} × … × GL_{n_t}, the trace tr(f_{τ,h} | π) is computed from the traces of the functions f_{τ,h_i} of the smaller groups on π_i (Scholze 2010 Lemmas 6.1–6.3); hence, if Theorem 1.2 holds for all n′ < n, the character identity of ET.6/scholze-local-langlands (a) holds for π with σ(π) = σ(π_1) ⊕ … ⊕ σ(π_t) (Theorem 6.4). (c) (Reduction by types) If (o) Theorem 1.2(a),(b) hold for all n′ < n, (i) the identity holds for all properly induced π, and (ii) for every essentially square-integrable or generalised Speh π there is a ℚ-linear combination rec(π) of representations with non-negative coefficients, total dimension n, satisfying the trace identity, and (iii) for supercuspidal π this rec_un(π) is a ℤ-linear virtual representation, then Theorem 1.2(a),(b) hold for n; the proof uses the theory of types to find h with prescribed traces on tempered representations and Kazhdan's density theorem (Scholze 2010 Lemmas 3.1–3.2).
hypotheses: induction on n
F finite over ℚ_p
proofSteps: (a): analyse the étale part of the universal deformation and Drinfeld structures (Scholze 2010 §5).

(b): compute the twisted trace of φ_{τ,h} on the base change of an induced representation by the Jacquet module along the parabolic, matching the connected–étale decomposition (Scholze 2010 §6; SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.2/jacquet-module, SR.2/geometric-lemma).
(c): Bernstein centre and types (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.3/bernstein-centre-blocks) with Kazhdan's density theorem (Scholze 2010 §3).

Condition (iii) is essential: positivity with rational coefficients alone does not make a genuine representation. ET.6/lubin-tate-comparison supplies integrality independently of the completed local correspondence.
acceptance: For n = 1 there is no proper Levi and (b) is vacuous.
For π = χ_1 × χ_2 an irreducible principal series of GL_2, (b) gives σ(π) = σ(χ_1) ⊕ σ(χ_2).
Condition (ii) of (c) only asks for a ℚ-linear combination with non-negative coefficients, not yet a representation.

nodes.title: Comparison of the test functions with deformation spaces of (O, D′)-groups
nodes.statement: For a semisimple D′ over ℚ_p with maximal order O_{D′}, an (O, D′)-group is a p-divisible group H with O_D^op = M_n(O)^op × O_{D′}^op-action decomposing as H_n × H′ with H_n of the type of ET.6/drinfeld-level-deformation-spaces and H′ étale. (a) The deformation space R_H of such an H is canonically R_β, and its level-m version R_{H,m} ≅ R_{β,m} × (H′[p^m])^× (Scholze 2010 Proposition 7.3); (b) Rψ_H ≅ Rψ_β ⊗ C_c^∞(O_{D′}^×) W_{F_r} × G_D(ℤ_p)-equivariantly (Corollary 7.4); (c) for any τ, h, h′ the function φ_{τ,h,h′} built from Rψ_H is associated with f^∨_{τ,h} ⊗ h′ (Lemma 7.5). This is the local input that lets the test function at p of the Shimura varieties of ET.6/division-algebra-shimura-varieties be expressed through φ_{τ,h}.

The displayed product for R_{H,m} is a fibre product over R_β after the étale torsion factor is canonically lifted. The associated function is on GL_n(F)×(D′)×, a tensor product; h×h′ is not an input to the GL_n construction.
proofSteps: Scholze 2010 Definition 7.1, Propositions 7.2–7.3, Corollary 7.4, Lemma 7.5: decompose the Dieudonné module along the O_D-action and identify deformations of H with deformations of H_n.

For H′ étale, deforming H′ is trivial, which is why only a factor (H′[p^m])^× appears.

nodes.title: Shimura varieties of the division-algebra unitary groups at Drinfeld level
nodes.statement: With the data (F = F_0K, D, *, G) of ET.4/simple-division-algebra-trace-identity (Scholze 2010 Lemma 8.1), a prime p split in K and a place w of F above p with F_w ≅ the given p-adic field, G(ℚ_p) ≅ GL_n(F_w) × (D′)^× × ℚ_p^× with D′ the product of the other local factors. For K^p ⊂ G(𝔸_f^p) small and m ≥ 0, the PEL moduli problem of abelian varieties with D-action, polarization, prime-to-p level K^p and Drinfeld level-ϖ^m structure on the one-dimensional part of the p-divisible group is representable by a projective scheme Sh_{K^p,m} over O_{F_w}, flat, with smooth generic fibre equal to the canonical model of the Shimura variety of (G, h^{-1}) at level K^p × K_{p,m}, and its completed local rings at closed points are the spaces R_{β,m} (ET.6/drinfeld-level-deformation-spaces) times the étale part (Scholze 2010 Lemma 9.2); the cohomology H_ξ = Σ_i (−1)^i lim H^i(Sh ⊗ ℚ̄, L_ξ) carries commuting actions of G(𝔸_f) and Gal(F̄_w/F_w), and π_*Rψ F_{K^p,m} ≅ (π_*Rψ ℚ̄_ℓ) ⊗ F_{K^p,0} (Lemma 9.1).
hypotheses: D a division algebra; signature (1, n−1) at one infinite place; p split in K; K^p small

Use exactly the auxiliary field, signature and division-place conditions of ET.4/simple-division-algebra-trace-identity; w differs from x,xᶜ. The level-zero model is smooth. Drinfeld-level local factors and the coefficient comparison require the formal-geometric suppliers recorded as gaps.
proofSteps: Representability and the generic fibre: PEL moduli of PELModuli:M2/representability, M4/canonical-model-identification, extended to Drinfeld level at w by the determinant condition (Scholze 2010 §8, citing Kottwitz and Harris–Taylor Lemma III.1.2).
Properness: D division (PELModuli:M2/properness-when-division).
Local structure: Serre–Tate and the comparison of ET.6/comparison-of-two-functions identify completed local rings with R_{β,m} (Scholze 2010 Lemmas 9.1–9.2).
acceptance: At m = 0 the integral model is smooth over O_{F_w}.
The relative dimension is n − 1.
For n = 1 the completed local rings are the Lubin–Tate rings of ET.6/drinfeld-level-deformation-spaces.
Replacing D by a split algebra leaves the hypotheses of this construction. Division proves properness here; splitting alone does not prove every other unitary Shimura datum nonproper.

nodes.title: The Langlands–Kottwitz point count at Drinfeld level
nodes.statement: With Sh_{K^p,m} and H_ξ as in ET.6/division-algebra-shimura-varieties, for τ ∈ Frob^j I_{F_w}, h ∈ C_c^∞(GL_n(O_{F_w})), h′ ∈ C_c^∞(O_{D′}^×) and f^p ∈ C_c^∞(G(𝔸_f^p)): tr(τ × h^∨ × h′ × e_{ℤ_p^×} × f^p | [H_ξ]) = Σ_{(γ_0;γ,δ)} c(γ_0;γ,δ) O_γ(f^p) TO_{δσ_0}(φ_{τ,h,h′} × e_{p^{−1}W(κ_r)^×}) tr(γ_0 | ξ), the sum over Kottwitz triples with vanishing Kottwitz invariant, and consequently n·tr(τ × h^∨ × h′ × e × f^p | [H_ξ]) = tr(f^∨_{τ,h} ⊗ h′ × e′ × f^p | [H_ξ]) (Scholze 2010 Theorem 9.3 and Corollary 9.4).
hypotheses: τ over a positive power of geometric Frobenius
the hypotheses of ET.6/division-algebra-shimura-varieties

Write r′=[κ(F_w):𝔽_p] and r=j r′. Normalize e as the characteristic idempotent of ℤ_p× and e′ as the characteristic idempotent of p^(−j r′)ℤ_p×. The point-count coefficients c(γ₀;γ,δ) use the ordinary Shimura Kottwitz-triple weights, not the Igusa indexing set of Shin 2009. An explicit lower-tier supplier for those weights is still required.
proofSteps: Apply the Fujiwara–Varshavsky trace formula (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.8/fujiwara-varshavsky-trace-formula) to the Frobenius-twisted Hecke correspondences on Sh_{K^p,m} ⊗ 𝔽̄ with coefficients π_*Rψ (Scholze 2010 §9; Varshavsky Theorem 2.3.2).
Compute local terms at fixed points through the completed local rings (ET.6/division-algebra-shimura-varieties) and ET.6/comparison-of-two-functions, giving twisted orbital integrals of φ_{τ,h,h′}.

Parametrise isogeny classes of points by Kottwitz triples using Honda–Tate theory (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuliPartII:F3/honda-tate) and Kottwitz's arguments for PEL varieties (Kottwitz 1992), which Scholze checks apply at Drinfeld level (Scholze 2010 p. 23).

Stabilisation is trivial for these groups (ET.4/simple-division-algebra-trace-identity), and the twisted orbital integrals become orbital integrals of f^∨_{τ,h} ⊗ h′ by ET.6/norm-maps-and-base-change-identities (Corollary 9.4).
acceptance: For m = 0 and h = 1, φ_{τ,h} is Kottwitz's φ_j and the identity is Kottwitz's point count at good reduction.
The normalising factor on the left side of Corollary 9.4 is Scholze's; a consumer takes it from there and does not set it to 1.
Without the vanishing of the Kottwitz invariant, a triple contributes no points.

nodes.statement: (a) For π_f occurring in ξ-cohomology, with multiplicity a(π_f), π_p=π_w⊗π_{w^p}⊗π_{p,0} and π_{p,0} unramified, Scholze Corollary 10.1 gives tr(f^∨_{τ,h}|π_w)=a(π_f)⁻¹ tr(τ|[W_ξ(π_f)]⊗χ_{π_{p,0}}) tr(h^∨|π_w). The unramified character χ evaluates the correctly normalized central p-power. The cohomological multiplicity is not silently replaced by 1. (b) Theorem 10.2 globalizes an unramified twist of every essentially square-integrable or generalized Speh π; its local component need not equal π before twisting. Corollary 10.3 produces rec_un(π), a ℚ-linear combination of W_F-representations with nonnegative coefficients and total dimension n satisfying the character identity. This is the early positive input to Lemma 3.2, before integrality and bijectivity.

Π conjugate self-dual, regular algebraic, square-integrable at x
proofSteps: Combine the point-count identity and the simple trace formula; keep the contragredient, similitude twist and multiplicity a(π_f) (Corollary 10.1 p. 26).

nodes.title: Scholze's characterization of the local Langlands correspondence
nodes.statement: For each irreducible smooth π of GL_n(F), there is a unique n-dimensional semisimple W_F-representation rec_un(π) with tr(f_{τ,h}|π)=tr(τ|rec_un(π))tr(h|π), for τ over positive powers of geometric Frobenius and rational-valued h∈C_c^∞(GL_n(O)). Define σ(π)=rec_un(π)⊗|·|^((1−n)/2). For any irreducible subquotient of normalized induction, σ is the direct sum of the inducing σ-parameters. These are Scholze Theorem 1.2(a),(b), equivalently Theorem 2.7(a),(b). Bijectivity and factors are separate later targets ET.6/supercuspidal-bijection and ET.6/l-epsilon-of-pairs. The symbol rec_F in ET.6/full-wd-local-langlands denotes the normalized full Weil–Deligne parameter, not rec_un.
hypotheses: F a finite extension of ℚ_p (characteristic 0)
ℓ ≠ p and a fixed isomorphism ℚ̄_ℓ ≅ ℂ
proofSteps: Induct on n using the complete reduction of Lemma 3.2: harmonic descent for induced representations, ET.6/global-galois-input for positive rational rec_un and ET.6/lubin-tate-comparison for integrality on supercuspidals.

Use Lemma 3.1 and density to extend the identity to all irreducibles; positive Frobenius traces determine the semisimple representation. This stage does not use the later bijectivity or pair-factor theorem.

For the Steinberg representation of GL_2, σ(St) = 1 ⊕ |·| up to the twist convention, the semisimplification of Sp_2 (monodromy is invisible to (a)).
rec is not injective on all irreducibles: π and its Zelevinsky dual have the same semisimple parameter (e.g. trivial and Steinberg of GL_2).

nodes.title: Relation to the Lubin–Tate tower
nodes.statement: Let [Rψ] be the alternating sum of global sections of nearby cycles of the Lubin–Tate tower, a virtual representation of GL_n(O)×(D××W_F)^0, where the superscript 0 is the valuation-zero kernel; compactly induce in D××W_F to obtain [Rψ̃] on GL_n(O)×D××W_F. (a) Each R^iψ is an admissible smooth representation of GL_n(O), smooth for O_D^×, continuous for I_F, and vanishes outside 0 ≤ i ≤ n−1 (Scholze 2010 Theorem 11.1). (b) φ_{τ,h}(β) = tr(τ × d^{-1} × h^∨ | [Rψ]) for d the element of D^× attached to β (Proposition 11.2). (c) If ρ is an irreducible representation of D^× with π = JL(ρ) supercuspidal (ET.6/local-jacquet-langlands), then as virtual GL_n(O) × W_F-representations [Rψ̃](ρ^∨) = (−1)^{n−1} π^∨|_{GL_n(O)} ⊗ rec_un(π) (Corollary 11.3); consequently rec_un(π) of a supercuspidal π is a ℤ-linear combination of representations (Corollary 11.5, using newvectors). The statement is a virtual identity over GL_n(O); the full GL_n(F) × W_F-equivariant concentration in one degree is the separate two-tower realisation of ET.6a.
hypotheses: π supercuspidal for (c); the Jacquet–Langlands correspondence of ET.6/local-jacquet-langlands
The valuation-zero subgroup is {(d,τ):v_D(d)+v_W(τ)=0}; a division uniformizer and geometric Frobenius both have valuation 1.
proofSteps: (a): Berkovich's comparison for formal schemes and Harris–Taylor Lemma II.2.8 (Scholze 2010 Theorem 11.1).
(b): compare the definition of φ_{τ,h} with the Lubin–Tate tower, which does not depend on β after base change to k̄ (Proposition 11.2).

Apply the early positive rational identity of ET.6/global-galois-input to supercuspidal π, use tempered cyclic base change and classical Jacquet–Langlands, and compare the division-algebra integral (Proposition 11.2, Corollary 11.3). This proof does not assume ET.6/scholze-local-langlands. Newvectors give a multiplicity-one GL_n(O)-type and hence integral coefficients (Corollary 11.5 p. 30); the required primary newvector supplier is a gap.
acceptance: For n = 1, [Rψ] is the Lubin–Tate realisation of local class field theory.
For n = 2 and ρ trivial on D^×, JL(ρ) is the Steinberg representation (not supercuspidal), so (c) does not apply.
The sign (−1)^{n−1} is the Kottwitz sign of D^×.

nodes.title: Bijectivity on supercuspidal representations
nodes.statement: The normalized σ of ET.6/scholze-local-langlands satisfies naturality and all five conditions of Scholze Theorem 12.1, including unramified parameter ⇒ Iwahori-fixed vectors. Hence it is a functorial extension of class field theory (Definition 12.2). For any such extension, its restriction to supercuspidals is injective with image exactly the irreducible n-dimensional representations of W_F (Theorem 12.3).
hypotheses: F finite over ℚ_p
proofSteps: Rank one and induction are available from the construction. Twisting and supercuspidal prime-degree cyclic base change use the later global-Galois identity after the character identity has been proved. For the Iwahori condition reduce to supercuspidals of n≥2 and show σ(π)^I=0 using the basic Lubin–Tate trace and absence of O_D×-invariants (Scholze pp. 30–31).

Theorem 12.3 pp. 31–32 proves both directions constructively. Condition (v) supplies a finite chain of cyclic extensions; at the first nonsupercuspidal base change use the full Galois orbit from AC Lemma 6.10 and induction in rank. For existence start with an irreducible Weil representation, lift its first reducible restriction using AC Theorem 6.2, and descend the chain, correcting character twists. AC Proposition 6.7 supplies uniqueness. No numerical equality of bounded-conductor counts is invoked.
acceptance: For n = 1 the statement is local class field theory.
For n = 2 and p odd, dihedral supercuspidals correspond to induced representations Ind_{W_E}^{W_F} χ.
σ(Steinberg) is reducible, consistent with Steinberg not being supercuspidal.

nodes.title: Harris's non-Galois automorphic induction
nodes.statement: A cuspidal Π on GL_n over a number field is potentially abelian when an n-dimensional representation Σ of the global Weil group is associated to Π at every finite and infinite place (Scholze Definition 13.1 p. 32); agreement at almost all places alone is weaker. Lemmas 13.3–13.4 p. 33 construct ℓ-adic realizations of algebraic Σ. For the CM datum, Π conjugate self-dual, regular L-algebraic and Π_x supercuspidal, Theorem 13.5(i) p. 34 upgrades association at infinity and almost all finite places to all finite places. Part (ii) descends potential abelianity along prime-degree cyclic F′/F when x has exactly one extension x′ and Π′_{x′} is supercuspidal. In Theorem 13.6 p. 34 let F₃⁰⊃F₂⁰⊃F₁⁰ be totally real of even degree over ℚ with F₃⁰/F₁⁰ solvable Galois, F_i=F_i⁰K for an imaginary quadratic K, and n=[F₂⁰:F₁⁰]. Choose x of F₁ split over F₁⁰ and inert in F₃. Require χ⁻¹=χ∘c, χ_τ(z)=z^{p_τ}z̄^{−p_τ} with distinct integral p_τ, and Stab_{Gal(F₃/F₁)}(χ_x∘Norm_{F₃/F₂})=Gal(F₃/F₂). Then there is a potentially abelian cuspidal induction on GL_n/F₁ associated at every place to Ind_{W_{F₂}}^{W_{F₁}}χ. An arbitrary algebraic χ without these hypotheses is not covered.
hypotheses: CM fields with totally real subfields of even degree; solvable Galois closure
proofSteps: Use the archimedean dictionary and ℓ-adic realizations of algebraic Hecke characters in Lemmas 13.3–13.4; these require explicit suppliers, recorded as gaps.
Theorem 13.5 uses Chebotarev and the post-correspondence Galois system, with the supercuspidal place choosing the extension uniquely.

Induct on the solvable tower using cyclic base change and induction. The stabilizer condition controls cuspidality at x, and the distinct archimedean weights ensure regularity (Theorem 13.6 pp. 34–35).
acceptance: For n = 1 the induction is the Hecke character itself.
For F^3_0 = F^2_0 Galois over F^1_0, the result reduces to cyclic or solvable automorphic induction.
A non-algebraic Hecke character has no ℓ-adic realisation, so (a) needs regular L-algebraicity.

nodes.title: Compatibility of the correspondence with L- and ε-factors of pairs
nodes.statement: The correspondence π ↦ σ(π) on supercuspidal representations (extended additively to the Grothendieck group of W_F) has the following properties: (i) in degree 1 it is local class field theory; (ii) σ(π ⊗ χ) = σ(π) ⊗ σ(χ); (iii) σ(π^∨) = σ(π)^∨; (iv) det σ(π) = σ(ω_π); (v) for supercuspidal π_1, π_2, L(s, π_1 × π_2) = L(s, σ(π_1) ⊗ σ(π_2)) and ε(s, π_1 × π_2, ψ) = ε(s, σ(π_1) ⊗ σ(π_2), ψ), with the Jacquet–Piatetski-Shapiro–Shalika factors on the left (AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.3/rs-local-factor) and the Deligne–Langlands factors on the right (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/local-epsilon-factor). Consequently it is the correspondence characterised by Henniart, and part (iii) follows from (v) by comparing poles.
hypotheses: π₁ and π₂ are supercuspidal. This node does not assert the extension to arbitrary irreducibles; ET.6/full-wd-local-langlands records the separate segment-pair and monodromy input.
proofSteps: Globalise π_1, π_2 as local components of potentially abelian cuspidal representations Π_1, Π_2 over a CM field with all other ramified components controlled (Scholze 2010 Lemma 14.2, using ET.6/non-galois-automorphic-induction and automorphic induction of Hecke characters).

Compare the global functional equations of L(s, Π_1 × Π_2) (AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.3/rs-global-functional-equation) and of the Artin–Hecke L-function of Σ_1 ⊗ Σ_2, whose local factors agree at all other places by construction; twist by highly ramified characters (Henniart's method) to separate the remaining place (Scholze 2010 Theorem 14.1 and proof).
acceptance: For n_1 = n_2 = 1 (v) is Tate's local functional equation (AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.1/local-functional-equation).
For π_2 the trivial character of GL_1, (v) gives the Godement–Jacquet factors of π_1 (AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.2/godement-jacquet-functional-equation).
L(s, π × π^∨) has a pole at s = 0, matching the trivial constituent of σ(π) ⊗ σ(π)^∨.

nodes.title: The local Langlands correspondence for GL_n with full Weil–Deligne parameters
nodes.statement: Let F be a finite extension of ℚ_p. There is a unique family of bijections rec_F : Irr(GL_n(F)) → {n-dimensional Frobenius-semisimple Weil–Deligne representations of W_F}, n ≥ 1, such that: (a) on supercuspidals rec_F = σ (ET.6/supercuspidal-bijection), with N = 0; (b) for a segment Δ = [ρ, ν^{k−1}ρ], rec_F(L(Δ)) = rec_F(ρ) ⊗ Sp_k (ET.6/segment-wd-parameter); (c) for a multisegment m, rec_F(L(m)) = ⊕_{Δ∈m} rec_F(L(Δ)), L(m) the Langlands quotient (ET.6/zelevinsky-classification); then rec_F is bijective, compatible with twists, central characters (det), contragredients, and L- and ε-factors of pairs (defined on the Galois side through Weil–Deligne representations with monodromy), and conductors (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.3/conductor-of-a-weil-deligne-representation). (d) The restriction of rec_F(π) to W_F, semisimplified, is σ(π) of ET.6/scholze-local-langlands; equivalently the semisimple Langlands parameter of rec_F(π) (ET.6/semisimple-langlands-parameter) is the point of the Bernstein centre of π. (e) The Steinberg representation St_n = L([ν^{(1−n)/2}, ν^{(n−1)/2}]) corresponds to |·|^{(1−n)/2} ⊗ Sp_n; an unramified principal series corresponds to the sum of unramified characters with its Satake parameters (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.4/spherical-parameter); generic π correspond to Weil–Deligne representations with no two blocks linked. Equal-characteristic local fields are not covered.
hypotheses: F of characteristic 0 (equal-characteristic F requires a separately checked construction)
Art_F normalised by geometric Frobenius
proofSteps: Define rec_F by (a)–(c); bijectivity from ET.6/segment-wd-parameter and ET.6/zelevinsky-classification (multisegments ↔ irreducibles ↔ Frobenius-semisimple Weil–Deligne representations).
Compatibility of the semisimplification with σ: ET.6/scholze-local-langlands (b) and the cuspidal support of L(m) (ET.6/zelevinsky-classification (f)).

The general pair-factor and conductor conclusions require an additional essentially-square-integrable segment-pair formula, with ker N and the monodromy correction, followed by multiplicativity across Langlands blocks. Multiplicativity over individual cuspidal support does not supply it: St₂ and the trivial representation have identical semisimple support but different ker N. ET.6/l-epsilon-of-pairs proves only the supercuspidal case. The missing primary proof and explicit supplier are recorded as a real gap, rather than claimed as a reduction already completed.
Uniqueness: Henniart's characterization on supercuspidals and the forced extension by (b)–(c).
acceptance: rec_F(trivial of GL_2) = |·|^{-1/2} ⊕ |·|^{1/2} (N = 0) and rec_F(St_2) = |·|^{-1/2} ⊗ Sp_2 with N ≠ 0: the two differ only by N.
For n = 1, rec_F is local class field theory.
rec_F(π^∨) = rec_F(π)^∨ on a supercuspidal π of GL_2 with non-trivial central character.

nodes.title: Semisimple Langlands parameters, also for inner forms of Levi subgroups
nodes.statement: (a) The semisimple Langlands parameter of a Frobenius-semisimple Weil–Deligne representation, viewed as W_F × SL_2(ℂ) → GL_m(ℂ), is its restriction along w ↦ (w, diag(|w|^{1/2}, |w|^{−1/2})); for π irreducible of GL_m(F) set σ_π^{ss} = this restriction of rec_F(π). It is compatible with normalised parabolic induction and depends only on the cuspidal support: it is exactly a point of the Bernstein centre, and non-trivial extensions exist only between irreducibles with the same semisimple parameter. (b) For J an inner form of a Levi subgroup M of GL_m(F) (for instance J_{b_v}(F_v) of ET.5/jb-endoscopic-levi-data) and π an irreducible smooth representation of J, the semisimple L-parameter σ_π : W_F → GL_m(ℚ̄_ℓ) is defined through the irreducible Langlands-quotient map Q of ET.6/inner-form-langlands-parameter followed by (a).

Use inner-form Langlands standard data, transfer its square-integrable factors by JL and take the split Langlands quotient Q (ET.6/inner-form-langlands-parameter). Apply rec_F and then restrict to the semisimple Weil representation. Badulescu’s additive LJ is not inverted.

σ^{ss} is not injective on irreducibles (trivial and Steinberg of GL_2 share it), so it cannot replace rec_F.

nodes.title: The local Jacquet–Langlands correspondence for inner forms of GL_n
nodes.statement: Let D be a central division algebra of dimension d² over F, n = rd and G′ = GL_r(D), an inner form of GL_n(F) with Kottwitz sign e(G′) = (−1)^{n−r} (ET.0/kottwitz-sign). Regular semisimple g′ ∈ G′ and g ∈ GL_n(F) correspond if they have the same characteristic polynomial. There is a unique bijection JL from essentially square-integrable irreducible representations of GL_r(D) to essentially square-integrable irreducible representations of GL_n(F) such that Θ_{JL(π′)}(g) = (−1)^{n−r} Θ_{π′}(g′) for all corresponding regular elliptic g, g′ (characters as functions, ET.4/padic-character-distributions). JL preserves central characters, commutes with twists by characters (det or reduced norm), and is compatible with contragredients. For r = 1, JL is a bijection from all irreducible representations of D^× to the essentially square-integrable representations of GL_n(F), and sends the trivial representation of D^× to the Steinberg representation; for n = 2 the sign is −1.
hypotheses: F of characteristic 0 (Deligne–Kazhdan–Vignéras; Badulescu in positive characteristic, not used)
proofSteps: Deligne–Kazhdan–Vignéras, via the simple trace formula comparison for GL_n and D^× and the transfer of functions of ET.3/inner-form-transfer; recorded at ET.3/inner-form-transfer (b) for tempered representations.
Extension to essentially square-integrable representations by twisting; characters as functions by ET.4/padic-character-distributions.

Badulescu §2 Theorem 2.1 pp. 3–4 records the general GL_r(D) correspondence; Scholze’s D× case alone does not supply all r. A complete primary proof of classical JL is still an imported-theory requirement.

For d = 1 (D = F) JL is the identity.

nodes.title: Badulescu's Langlands–Jacquet map on Grothendieck groups
nodes.statement: For G′=GL_r(D), n=rd, Badulescu defines a surjective additive map LJ_r:Groth(GL_n(F))→Groth(G′) by the standard-module basis. Every essentially square-integrable representation of GL_n(F) transfers uniquely by classical JL, and LJ_r(JL(δ′))=δ′. Characters satisfy Θ_{LJ_r(V)}(g′)=(−1)^(n−r)Θ_V(g) on all corresponding regular semisimple elements. The kernel is spanned by standard representations induced from Levis that do not transfer to G′. The family over all r commutes with normalized induction and Jacquet functors for corresponding Levis, as the Hopf-algebra quotient of Theorem 3.6. For a generic irreducible product of square-integrable factors, LJ is zero if the inducing Levi does not transfer; otherwise it is the irreducible product of their JL inverses (Proposition 3.3). In particular generic principal series vanish for d>1. LJ is an additive Grothendieck-group map, not a bijection of irreducibles or the map used to attach inner-form parameters. This 2007 source states the general signed-irreducibility assertion only as Conjecture 3.11; it is not imported as a theorem here.
hypotheses: F of characteristic 0
D a central division algebra; inner forms of products of general linear groups
proofSteps: Use the Langlands standard-module bases of Badulescu §2.1–2.2 pp. 5–6. His additive injection JL_r of Theorem 3.1 pp. 9–10 extends classical JL; Proposition 3.2 p. 11 gives the quotient LJ_r and its all-regular-semisimple character identity.

The kernel description makes the map surjective. Across all ranks the quotient is compatible with product and coproduct (Theorem 3.6 pp. 13–15); each displayed Jacquet or induction identity must use corresponding Levis.
Apply Proposition 3.3 p. 11 for generic irreducibles. Generic principal series use a diagonal split Levi, which does not transfer when d>1. This is not a proof by elliptic characters alone.
acceptance: LJ(χ_1 × χ_2) = 0 for an irreducible principal series; a map sending irreducibles to non-zero irreducibles would be wrong.
For d = 1 the map is the identity of Groth(GL_n(F)).

nodes.title: Generic principal series parameters do not transfer to non-split inner forms
nodes.statement: Let J be a non-quasi-split inner form of a Levi M of GL_m(F) (for example J_{b_v}(F_v) when b_v has a non-integral slope), and λ = χ_1 ⊕ … ⊕ χ_m a semisimple parameter that is a sum of characters with χ_i χ_j^{-1} ≠ |·|^{±1} for i ≠ j (a generic principal series parameter). Then no irreducible smooth representation π of J has σ_π = λ (ET.6/semisimple-langlands-parameter), and LJ_M(π_M) = 0 for every irreducible π_M of M whose parameter is λ. Consequently, if a representation π_p^n⃗ of an endoscopic group of a unitary group transfers at a place p_i to a generic principal series of GL_n(F_{p_i}) while J_{b_i} is a non-quasi-split inner form of M_{b_i}, then Red^b_n⃗(π^n⃗_p) = 0 (Caraiani–Scholze 2017 Lemma 5.4.3).
hypotheses: J not quasi-split
λ generic in the stated sense
proofSteps: Use Q and the inner-form Langlands data. If λ is a sum of characters with no distinct ratio |·| or |·|⁻¹, no monodromy chain of length at least 2 can join its characters. Thus every split square-integrable standard factor would have degree 1. A nonsplit GL_s(D) factor transfers square-integrable data of dimension sd with d>1, and such degree-one data cannot occur. This proves absence of λ for the nonsplit inner factor. Separately, Proposition 3.3 kills the generic principal series induced from the nontransferring split diagonal Levi. Vanishing under LJ alone does not prove parameter absence.

For Red^b: the L-morphism ^LM_{G_n⃗} → ^LM_b restricts η̃, so the image of π^n⃗_p in Groth(M_b(ℚ_p)) has only generic principal series components at p_i, which lie in the kernel of LJ (Caraiani–Scholze 2017 proof of Lemma 5.4.3).

If J is quasi-split (J = M) the statement is false: the principal series itself has parameter λ.
If χ_1χ_2^{-1} = |·|, the parameter is that of Steinberg/trivial and does transfer to D^×.

nodes.title: Explicit local Langlands and Jacquet–Langlands in level zero
nodes.statement: Use the specific setting of Newton–Thorne Lemma 3.6: n=2m, q≡−1 (mod p) for an odd auxiliary prime p distinct from the residue characteristic, D/F of degree n, and a character χ of order p of 𝔽_{q²}×. Inflate χ∘Norm_{𝔽_{qⁿ}/𝔽_{q²}} to a character σ of O_D×. If σ occurs in ρ|O_D× for an irreducible ρ of D×, the composite of classical JL and full LLC places JL(ρ) in the Bernstein component specified by the type τ_s (Newton–Thorne proof of Lemma 3.6 p. 18). This node does not give a general degree-n induced parameter for every depth-zero ρ: for example 1_{D×} transfers to St_n and has nonzero monodromy. The explicit Bushnell–Henniart rectifier formulas needed for a general level-zero theorem were not independently read and remain a gap.

proofSteps: Apply the explicitly cited composite LLC/JL calculation to this residue-field norm character, as in Newton–Thorne Lemma 3.6 p. 18. The underlying Bushnell–Henniart formula and its generalization must be checked from its primary source before closing the gap.
acceptance: For n = 1 the statement is the tame part of local class field theory.

nodes.title: p-adic types with field action
nodes.statement: For a number field F₀ define a p-adic type as (M,(η_t),(n_t),κ), where M=∏_{t∈I} M_t is a nonempty finite product of CM or totally real fields, κ:F₀→M is a ℚ-algebra homomorphism, n_t is a positive integer, and η_t=Σ_{x|p}η_{t,x}[x] is an effective rational divisor supported above p with η_t+c*η_t=[p]. Here [p] has coefficient e(x/p), and pullback under a field embedding uses the ramification indices. It is simple when I is a singleton and n_t=1. Equivalence is common refinement by F₀-algebra embeddings, preserving the pulled-back η and summing multiplicities in each target factor as in Shin §8 p. 24; isomorphism and equivalence are distinct. Each equivalence class has a unique minimal representative up to isomorphism.
hypotheses: M_t CM or totally real; κ is an algebra map, not a polarization or positivity datum.
proofSteps: Use divisor pullback with ramification multiplicities; common refinements give the equivalence relation.
For simple types descend η in a common Galois extension to its stabilizer field; then collect distinct minimal simple types and multiplicities (Shin §8 pp. 24–25).

nodes.title: Inner-form parameter through the Langlands quotient Q
nodes.statement: For π′ irreducible on GL_r(D), write it as the unique Langlands quotient of an ordered standard induction of essentially square-integrable δ′_i (Badulescu §2.1 p. 5). Let Q(π′) be the Langlands quotient of the split standard module with factors JL(δ′_i), with exactly the same real exponents (Badulescu §3.3 p. 15). Q is injective on irreducibles (Proposition 3.9 p. 16). Define rec_{G′}(π′)=rec_F(Q(π′)) and its semisimple parameter by restriction. For products of inner forms take direct sums. This is not an inverse of the Grothendieck-group map LJ: in the 2007 source LJ(Q(π′)) can contain lower terms, and equality is Conjecture 3.10. The split case is Q=id.

Retain its choice as data: it is not unique. Define Ram_ℚ(ϖ) as the finite set of rational primes below finite places where its local character is nontrivial on the units; every spherical transfer set S contains this set. At the complex place write ϖ∞(z)=(z/|z|)^m|z|^{it}; restriction to ℝ× forces m odd and t=0.
