nodes.title: Invariant orbital and character distributions on the twisted coset
nodes.statement: For a characteristic-zero local field k and the component 𝒢θ of 𝒢⋊⟨θ⟩, use the connected group 𝒢 for conjugation and θ-stable parabolic/Levi subsets. For a Levi subset Mθ, construct the twisted weighted orbital distribution J_M(δθ,f) using the component discriminant |det(1−Ad(δ)θ on 𝔤/𝔦_δθ)|^(1/2), connected centralizer quotient measure, and Arthur’s (𝒢,M)-family weight. Construct J_M(π,X,f) from normalized intertwining operators for the corresponding induced θ-stable representation, retaining its chosen extension. Define the maps φ_L from weighted characters and the invariant distributions recursively by I_M^𝒢=J_M^𝒢−Σ_{L⊊𝒢} Ĩ_M^L∘φ_L, in both orbital and spectral variables. Ĩ denotes descent to the invariant character quotient. At M=𝒢 the orbital distribution is the discriminant-normalized twisted orbital integral and the spectral distribution is the ordinary twisted character transform. The geometric test-function transfer uses unnormalized orbital integrals; convert by the displayed discriminant rather than identifying the two normalizations.
hypotheses: Measures, central character and normalized intertwiner are fixed; π is tempered for the initial spectral transform.
Functions are in Arthur’s smooth Hecke/almost-compact spaces on the component, K-finite at real places; the quotient is by functions whose twisted character transforms vanish.
The induction through lower-dimensional Levi subsets uses character support, provided by the separate twisted Paley–Wiener/character-support theorem.
proofSteps: Use the component kernel and the same truncation parameter/chambers as AS.6, transporting them to θ-stable parabolics; AS.6 supplies the untwisted machinery and does not assert these coset identities.

Construct weighted orbital integrals and weighted characters with the component discriminant and global/local intertwiner conventions. Arthur I §§2–3 defines the invariant recursion simultaneously on components.

Induct on the dimension of proper Levi subsets; character support makes the hatted distributions on the quotient well-defined. Arthur I Corollary 8.3 and Proposition 9.1 give the descent and splitting identities.
Use the two completions of Arthur II §5: Kottwitz–Rogawski supplies support on characters and Delorme–Mezo the real twisted trace transform. These complete the disconnected induction.
acceptance: For θ=1, the recursion agrees with AS.6, with the same measures and character quotient.
For M=𝒢 there is no proper-Levi subtraction.
Multiplying an order-two extension operator by −1 reverses its twisted spectral transform.

nodes.title: Twisted character support and real Paley–Wiener theorem
nodes.statement: For a component of a reductive group over a characteristic-zero local field with rational points, each invariant orbital distribution I_M(γ) is supported on characters: it vanishes on any Hecke function whose invariant twisted character transform is zero. The real twisted trace transform is onto the Paley–Wiener families of Delorme–Mezo Theorem 4: finite K-type support, covariance under the root-of-unity change of extension, and Fourier transforms of smooth functions supported in the radius-t ball on each induced spectral parameter space. Thus the real trace Paley–Wiener assumption left in Kottwitz–Rogawski and Arthur’s original disconnected induction is supplied for the components used here.
hypotheses: Use Delorme–Mezo’s real reductive component, chosen maximal compact group and radius convention; only representations whose restriction to the identity component is irreducible tempered enter its primary dual.
Kottwitz–Rogawski’s general support theorem assumes trace Paley–Wiener; the two results are used together, not cited as two unconditional proofs of the same statement.
proofSteps: Delorme–Mezo Theorem 4: necessity follows from finite K-types, the scalar extension action and the Fourier support bound. For sufficiency convert the family to the main Theorem 3 data; normalized analytic intertwiners preserve the root-of-unity covariance and the spectral relations.

Kottwitz–Rogawski §6: induct on dimension/Levi order, descend to regular elliptic elements, globalize the local group, use weak approximation and the cohomological conjugacy-separation lemmas, and isolate a positive multiple of the desired local distribution in the global trace identity.

The global argument is an induction in Arthur’s formula, not a cycle using this packet’s final unitary stable comparison. Its underlying approximation/Hasse inputs remain the precise source-proof gap.
acceptance: A family invariant under A↦−A with nonzero value cannot be the order-two twisted trace transform.
For θ=1, the covariance condition becomes the ordinary real trace transform condition.
If every twisted character vanishes on f, every I_M(γ,f) vanishes.

nodes.title: The archimedean invariant vanishing and character identity
nodes.statement: In Morel’s base-change component for a quasi-split cuspidal fixed group H with simply connected derived subgroup, let f∞ be a twisted pseudo-coefficient of the θ-discrete representation with parameter φ|W_ℂ, for the discrete-series packet associated with a regular algebraic coefficient of H. After splitting, a term for M can survive only when A_M=A_M,ℝ. For such M, I_M^𝒢(γ,f∞)=0 if the associated fixed Levi M_H is not cuspidal. If it is cuspidal, I_M^𝒢(γ,f∞)=|D^M(γ)|^(1/2) Φ_M^𝒢(γ,f∞), where the discriminant uses the semisimple part of γθ and Φ is the θ-discrete packet character expression of Morel §8.2. It is zero on non-θ-semisimple γ. These identities yield Morel Proposition 8.2.3; its spectral coefficients still incorporate discrete data from proper Levi subsets.
hypotheses: Use Morel’s hypotheses and central-character spaces; no claim for an arbitrary disconnected reductive group or arbitrary infinity function.
Real θ-discrete character growth and boundary identities, and connected centralizer unipotent limits, are needed; precise unread underlying proofs are a gap.
proofSteps: Apply Arthur I Proposition 9.1 and Corollary 9.2 to isolate the infinity factor and force equality of rational and real split centres.

For a noncuspidal associated fixed Levi, Morel Lemma 8.2.6 first descends a regular element to a proper real Levi and uses cuspidality. Local centralizer orbital integrals and their regular density extend zero to singular and unipotent elements.

For a cuspidal M, prove the regular character identity by induction on M using the differential equations, growth estimate and boundary relations for θ-discrete characters; the full-group case is Morel Lemma 8.1.10.

Use Morel Lemma 8.2.5 and connected-centralizer unipotent orbital limits to extend from regular semisimple elements. Substitute in the split geometric expansion. The separate global no-proper-cuspidal theorem then removes the proper geometric terms when [F⁺:ℚ]>1.
acceptance: For the full component the fixed Levi is H, which is cuspidal; testing cuspidality on complex GL_n would incorrectly erase this term.
A noncuspidal fixed Levi gives zero even at a singular semisimple element, not merely on the regular set.
At degree one a proper cuspidal fixed Levi may survive; infinity cuspidality alone does not imply the simple geometric identity.

sources.locator: §8.2 Proposition 8.2.3 and proof pp. 133–135; Lemmas 8.2.5/8.2.6 pp. 135–136; Lemma 8.1.10 p. 130
sources.match: Gives the component invariant vanishing proof and corrects the spectral expansion by retaining the proper-Levi discrete data.

nodes.title: Tempered local unitary packets with inner-twist pairings
nodes.statement: For a local field of characteristic zero, a quasi-split unitary group G*, an extended pure inner twist (G,ξ,z), and a bounded local L-parameter φ (Arthur SL₂ trivial), KMSW Theorem* 1.6.1 gives a finite relevant packet Π_φ(G,ξ) and pairing into Irr(S_φ♮,χ_z). It is empty if φ is irrelevant. Packet members are tempered, the pairing is injective, and at nonarchimedean places it is a bijection to the prescribed component characters. At real places the bijection is over the specified union of pure inner forms, not necessarily on a single form. The packet is independent of z while its pairing uses z. The normalized endoscopic character identity includes e(G) and evaluation at s_e s_φ, with transfer factors normalized by (ξ,z). At a split place the packet is the GL_N singleton.
hypotheses: Bounded L-parameters only, in the unconditional generic local case of KMSW v1; use the chosen Whittaker normalization and extended pure inner twist.
The GL local parameter dictionary is ET.6/full-wd-local-langlands at nonarchimedean places and AF.1/archimedean-llc-gln at real/complex places; the former retains its inherited factor proof gap.
proofSteps: Use the local classification and normalized endoscopic identity of KMSW §1.6.1; relevance and the central character χ_z determine which inner form receives each member.
Use the injectivity/bijection clauses with their field-dependent scope. Lemma 1.6.2 transports a change of z without claiming that its pairing is unchanged.

The proof passes through quasi-split classification and normalized local intertwining relations. Their exact primary proof chains are the classification gap, distinct from the packet statement itself.
acceptance: An irrelevant parameter gives the empty packet on that form.
At a split place the packet is a GL_N singleton; an independently chosen cyclic GL base-change fibre is not a unitary packet.
A real packet can be smaller than the full component-character set on one inner form; surjectivity is over the prescribed union.

sources.match: Pins the unconditional bounded-parameter packet, pairing, relevance, character identity and real-place union.

nodes.title: Extended local unitary packets by positive-exponent induction
nodes.statement: For ψ∈Ψ⁺(G*) write the KMSW §1.6.4 decomposition ψ=ψ_M·φ_λ with ψ_M bounded on a relevant Levi M* and λ in the positive chamber, giving an unramified character χ_λ. If the Levi datum is irrelevant for G, set Π_ψ(G,ξ)=∅. Otherwise transfer the extended pure inner twist to M and set Π_ψ(G,ξ)={I_P(π_M⊗χ_λ): π_M∈Π_ψM(M,ξ_M)}. Transport the pairing by Irr(S_ψ♮,χ_z)=Irr(S_ψM♮,χ_zM), using KMSW (1.6.3)–(1.6.4). These induced admissible representations may be reducible or nonunitary for a general Ψ⁺ parameter. Do not replace them by irreducible Langlands quotients without an additional theorem. For λ=0 and tempered ψ this recovers the tempered packet. Retain Weyl-conjugacy independence and the choice-sensitive pairing.
hypotheses: In the generic global localization used here the bounded Levi packet is a tempered L-packet. A general nongeneric bounded Arthur parameter would require the broader bounded packet theorem, whose proof is not claimed in this revision.
Normalize parabolic induction and χ_λ as in KMSW; the inner twist must be relevant for that Levi.
proofSteps: Separate positive real exponents from the bounded parameter and use the relevant Levi decomposition in KMSW §1.6.4.

Construct normalized induction from each bounded Levi packet member and transport its component-character pairing through (1.6.3)–(1.6.4). Record these as actual induced modules, preserving possible reducibility.

Weyl reordering of the linear factors and the canonical induced representation identifications give independence of the representative decomposition. A change of z transports the pairing via the central character, not literal equality of pairings.
acceptance: For λ=0 and bounded φ this is the tempered packet.
Irrelevant Levi data give the empty packet.
Taking Langlands quotients of a reducible induced member changes the stated construction and needs an extra theorem.

sources.match: Defines the extended induced packets and their pairings; explains their necessity even for generic global parameters.

nodes.title: Public cohomological unitary weak base change and descent
nodes.statement: Let E/F be CM with [F:ℚ]≥2 and U an inner form of the quasi-split unitary group in Labesse §5. Let σ be a discrete automorphic representation with discrete-series infinity component satisfying property (*): all representations with its finite part have infinity pseudo-coefficient trace of one common sign. Labesse Corollary 5.3 gives a weak base change to an isobaric sum of θ-stable discrete GL blocks, with local matching at unramified and split finite places and compatible infinitesimal character at infinity. If every block is cuspidal, the infinity component is its actual archimedean base change. Conversely, when E/F is unramified at all finite places and U is quasi-split at finite inert places, Theorem 5.4 descends a θ-stable cuspidal cohomological GL_N representation to a discrete cohomological σ. Under its extra discrete-series, spherical-inert and (*) hypotheses a cuspidal σ has multiplicity one. This is weak unitary base change with precisely these hypotheses; it does not prove all-place transfer in the separate Harris–Taylor division-algebra setting.
hypotheses: Use the central-character, inner-form and discrete infinity hypotheses of Labesse Theorem 5.1. Property (*) holds in the compact infinity case and with the sufficiently regular coefficients specified on p. 42; it is not assumed for every cohomological representation.
The converse retains the everywhere-finitely-unramified CM extension and finite-inert quasi-splitness hypotheses.
proofSteps: Labesse Theorem 5.1 compares the unitary trace to the twisted GL trace with the discrete-series test function and controlled endoscopic terms.
The common-sign property isolates the finite part without cancellation. Corollary 5.3 obtains a θ-stable discrete isobaric weak lift, with the precise split/unramified and infinity compatibilities.

For the converse Theorem 5.4 uses the additional finite-place hypotheses to match the cuspidal θ-stable GL trace and recover the cohomological unitary representation. Its multiplicity-one assertion uses the additional spherical-inert and (*) assumptions.
acceptance: At compact infinity, property (*) prevents cancellation of the finite part.
A residual discrete GL block does not imply actual infinity base change from infinitesimal-character compatibility alone.
A ramified finite inert place prevents direct application of the stated descent theorem.

sources.match: The public source gives this wider cohomological weak lift and a descent with stronger finite-place hypotheses; neither equals the restricted all-place HT theorem.
